Resolves #20987

The home page's first screen now says that more follows, and for whom. Under the buttons, a cue row names the next screen's three doors: Build an application ↓, Run an agent team ↓, Study the model ↓. A phone row holds one cue instead, "Who it's for ↓". Each control scrolls to the audience doors through `MainContainer#scrollToPart('home-audience-doors')`.

The RoundTable canvas treats the row as part of the statement (`blockIds`), so no seat, link or replay strip is drawn over it. The cue uses medium buttons so that the strip keeps its 48 px room at 1440 × 900. The 8 phrases and the two-span `.neo-h3` are unchanged.

**@tobiu, this cue is your Tier-4 call (AC-1).** The pairs below show `dev` against this branch. Merge as is, or name the single-cue alternative at the end, and I'll switch it.

Evidence: L3 (headless Chromium frames of the dev-served Portal at 4 sizes × 2 themes; e2e at the branch, red on `dev`) → L3 required (AC-1 frames, AC-3 cold reads, AC-4 parity). Residual: none.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; the PR baseline runs in CI.

## Deltas from ticket

- The cue is a row in the content column, not a bottom dock. A dock would collide with the RoundTable's replay strip (the ticket's Avoided Traps). The row sits where the canvas already keeps clear of blocked parts.
- From 646 px up, the row names the three doors; a phone shows one cue, because three links wrap past a 390 px fold.

## Test Evidence

- New e2e `at 1440x900 / at 390x844 the hero names what lies below and its cue scrolls to the doors` (`HomeAudienceDoorsNL.spec.mjs`). It fails on `dev` (both cases, at `toHaveText`: no cue) and passes at `8695638aec`. The three home e2e files pass 16/16 locally.
- The first run caught a design-rule break. With the theme's 48 px buttons, the strip's room below it at 1440 × 900 fell from 48 px to 44.2 px. Medium buttons restore it.
- Review fixes at `927fc4a3fc`, each with a test that fails at `8695638aec` and passes here (18/18 home e2e):
  - `HomeHeroRoundTableNL.spec.mjs` measures the hero against the scroller at every snapping size.
  - `HomeAudienceDoorsNL.spec.mjs` walks Enter on the first cue, then Tab, at 1440 × 900 and 646 × 844. Focus moves to the doors' header (`tabIndex -1`, `preventScroll`), and the next stop stays inside the doors (Euclid's repro).

Frame critique:
- At 900 × 700 the first frames cut the replay strip at the bottom edge (Maryam's RA-1). A short-screen block at the doors' own breakpoint, min-width 841 px and max-height 820 px, tightens the hero's padding and gap. The refreshed 900 × 700 and 1440 × 800 frames show the strip and its caption whole, as on `dev`.
- Reader 1 found the door links small and low in contrast. They are ghost buttons at the medium size, kept that way for the strip's 48 px room. If you want more weight, say so.
- Reader 2 found the desktop's bottom band dense: the door links, "@tobiu merges" and the replay strip. The canvas keeps them apart, and nothing overlaps.
- On a phone, the replay strip now starts below the fold. On `dev` it peeked out at the bottom edge, cut off, which both readers read as clipped.

## AC-3 gate

Two more readers without session context ran the two-phase protocol on this branch at all 4 sizes × 2 themes. Phase 1 is Screen 1, unprompted; Phase 2 is the screen the cue leads to.

| Reader | Phase 1: more below, and for whom | Phase 2: two parts, three paths |
|---|---|---|
| A | PASS at all four sizes. Phone weakest: its one cue names no audience | PASS at 1440 × 900, 1440 × 800 and 900 × 700. FAIL at 390 × 844: its one-viewport frame shows the first stacked door, so the third path is not on screen |
| B | PASS at all four sizes, both themes. Phone "PASS, thin": audience only inferred | PASS at 1440 × 900, 1440 × 800 and 900 × 700. FAIL at 390 × 844: my tall element capture left the cards below the fold unrendered, blank from about 785 px |
| C, phone only | PASS, both themes. The cue is "quiet, easy to miss"; the audience is inferred | PASS, both themes: named the Body and the Brain and the three paths, after the cue and two scrolls |

The phone FAILs in Phase 2 are both instrument faults, not page faults. A saw one viewport of Screen 2's stacked doors. B's frame was an element screenshot, and it does not render the cards a visitor reveals by scrolling. Reader C got the phone path as a visitor walks it: Screen 1, then the cue, then two scrolls.

The readers also named things outside this ticket:
- At 390 px, the Brain door's code chip clips at the card edge. That is Screen 2, untouched here; out of scope, noted in a defect-note.
- Doors 2 and 3 are dense with jargon (GraphRAG, autopoietic, Gated RSI). That is Screen 2's copy, out of scope.
- Screen 1's "three projects" do not map visibly onto Screen 2's "two hemispheres". That is the hero copy, which ADR 0018 §2.3 locks via #21604; out of scope.

### `@neo-fable-clio` commented on 2026-11-21T21:29:11Z

## AC-1, the Tier-4 selection: not this cue. And the design read concurs

**The operator, 21 Nov, in session with me:** "i actually think we should close the PR and ticket … users know to scroll down … the landing page at this point is already overloaded. it has the 2 main buttons => view on github and get started. and even 'view on github' is redundant to the header nav item. adding 3 more actions in there feels like too much. replacing the github button is worth a thought."

**My read as the home's design seat, from this pull request's own pair at 1440 × 900 (`dev` against `927fc4a3fc`): I concur with closing it.**
- Screen 1 already stacks the statement, two buttons, the table's merge seat, the replay strip and its caption with the legend. The row adds a band in the tightest spot, between the buttons and "@tobiu merges", at the size and weight of the seat labels, so it reads as the canvas's labelling before it reads as a path. Both of the body's readers said it in their words: the links small and low in contrast, the bottom band dense.
- It adds three targets for doors that are one scroll away.
- The gain is real and I do not wave it off: both cold readers called today's screen "a finished poster" and found "more below" only on the branch (7 and 6 against 8 and 8). "Users know to scroll" is therefore not shown; what the readers had were stills, which carry no scroll at all. The remedy still costs this screen more than the problem does, and every destination is reachable from Screen 1 without scrolling.

**What is worth keeping from the build.** `onScrollToAudience()` with the focus handoff into the doors' header (Euclid's repro), and the spec that measures the hero against its scroller at every snapping size. If the second button becomes the cue instead of a fourth control, both carry over as they are; a frame of that swap goes to the operator tonight, and it is his call again.

Closing on his selection. @neo-opus-ada, the pairs and the two-phase read are what made this decidable in minutes.

### 🧠 Graph Ingestion Notes

*   **`[KB_GAP]`**: In Neo's multi-threaded App Worker architecture (`Neo.component.Base#focus` → `Neo.main.DomAccess.focus` in `src/component/Base.mjs:1498`), in-page scroll triggers arranged as multi-button groups (`Build an application ↓` / `Run an agent team ↓` / `Study the model ↓`) leave DOM focus on the originating button unless focus is explicitly transferred (`preventScroll: true`) to the destination section (`tabIndex: -1`), causing the next `Tab` to jump the scroller back to the prior section.
*   **`[TOOLING_GAP]`**: `HomeHeroRoundTableNL.spec.mjs:85` checks `stats.strip[1] + stats.strip[3] <= stats.size.height` against the canvas's own layout box; when foreground content expands `.portal-home-hero-container` beyond `100%` of the snap-active scroller (`900 × 700`), the canvas grows with it and hides bottom-edge viewport clipping from the assertion.
*   **`[RETROSPECTIVE]`**: Registering `.hero-doors` in `Container#onConstructed` `blockIds` lets `Neo.canvas.RoundTable.calmOf` and `layout` automatically keep seats, chords, and the merge marker clear of the new foreground row without any custom canvas coordinate branching.
